title: RedCrest Claims — inference intake (raw)
content:
RAW NOTES FROM 2025-02-18 CUSTOMER CALL - RedCrest Insurance (internal)

Attendees:
- RedCrest: Anil Mehta (CTO), Priya Ramesh (ML infra lead), Jorge Alvarez (security)
- Redwood: Maya Cortez (SE), Ethan Park (Solutions Eng)

High-level ask:
- Replace current GKE-hosted endpoint with a private on-prem inference solution for claim-triage assistant.
- Hard SLOs for customer-facing agent: p95 end-to-end request <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms for typical payloads. Throughput target ~150 req/s (concurrent users peak) with 2k daily peak-concurrent sessions.
- Data residency + HIPAA-adjacent PII handling. VPC-only, no egress to public internet, KMS/HSM integration for key storage.

Context / constraints mentioned by customer (copied verbatim bits):
- "We cannot send claim text outside our VPC; logs must be retained internally for 90 days and accessible for audits."
- "We will be using our own on-prem GPU cluster (mixed: 2x A100 80GB, 6x T4s), want Redwood Private control plane but local runtime. Can we route to Dedicated if our cluster is saturated?"

Immediate technical requirements and preferences:
- Model family: prefer open weights. Their initial evaluation: Llama2-13B and a couple of instruction-finetuned 13B variants. Interested in quantized 4-bit (q4f16) to fit more replicas on T4s.
- Expected prompt size: average user prompt ~120 tokens + system + retrieved context ~800 tokens => typical request ~1000 tokens generation cap 256 tokens.
- Retrieval augmentation: vector DB (self-hosted Milvus) for retrieval; embeddings must be computed inside VPC.
- Audit logs: immutable stream to S3-compatible object store inside their network.
- Auth: mTLS between Redwood Private runtime and their fleet; support for HSM/KMS for signing and encryption keys (customer uses AWS CloudHSM on-prem).

Performance targets and rough capacity calc (back-of-envelope):
- Avg request tokens: ~120 in, 256 out max -> ~376 tokens per request. If model throughput on A100 (~2000 tokens/s for 13B float?) but quantized on T4 will be slower (~400–800 tok/s depending on kernels).
- For 150 req/s * 376 tok ≈ 56,400 tok/s required. With mixed hardware, plan to route majority to A100 nodes and spill to T4 pool. Consider autoscale/burst to cloud Dedicated if sustained > 60k tok/s.

Serving architecture options discussed:
1) Private deployment (preferred): Redwood Private control plane in Redwood cloud, runtime inside RedCrest VPC. Pros: meets VPC requirement, audit/log integration, lower egress. Cons: need mTLS + HSM integration work.
2) Dedicated hybrid: Have a small Redwood Dedicated pool to absorb bursts with encrypted transit. Requires legal sign-off for ephemeral egress.
3) Fully air-gapped: not feasible for initial phase (they want Redwood console for rollouts).

Implementation gotchas / friction points to follow up:
- KV cache: warm-up pattern will matter. If many cold sessions (claim-by-claim), cost/latency hit. Suggest prefix caching for common system prompts and claim templates.
- Batch sizing: their use-case is low-latency interactive triage — want aggressive limits on batch latency (max_latency_ms ~ 80ms). That reduces throughput gains from batching. Need to quantify tradeoffs with real samples.
- Quantization regressions: their QA requires output-stability tests; need eval harness with their golden prompt set to detect hallucination/regression from q4 -> must tie into Redwood Optimize pipeline.
- Embedding drift: since embeddings computed locally, we must ensure embedding model/version pinned and reproducible across nodes for similarity search stability.

Security & compliance items (explicit asks):
- HSM integration for root keys; bring-your-own-key (BYOK) enforced.
- Audit path: every inference request must log request-id, model-version, route, latency, and user-id to internal store.
- Data retention policy: 90d; ability to purge specific PII on request.
- Access controls: RBAC in console mapped to their AD groups (SAML/SCIM) - identity sync questions.

Benchmark plan (proposed):
- Phase 0 (lab): 1 A100, 1 T4, deploy Llama2-13B quantized q4f16 and float baseline. Run synthetic traffic using their golden prompt set (5000 requests) measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput.
- Phase 1 (staging in VPC): run with their Milvus instance + Milvus embedding flow. Validate end-to-end retrieval latencies and combined system latencies.
- Phase 2 (pilot): canary inside 10% of production traffic, monitor quality regressions and cost.

Action items / next steps (owners & rough dates):
- Maya: send initial SOW sketch + network diagram template by 2025-02-20.
- Ethan: produce lab benchmark matrix (A100 vs T4, q4 vs float) using sample prompts; target 2025-02-27.
- Priya (RedCrest): share golden prompt set (50–200 prompts), sample claim payloads, and access to a test Milvus by 2025-02-24.
- Security: schedule 1-hr deep dive with Jorge & Redwood security to confirm HSM/keyflow (target week of 2025-02-24).
- Legal/Compliance: Redwood GTM to prep draft DPA & contractual language for audit log retention and data residency; TBD owner from GTM.

Open questions to triage internally (must answer before lab run):
1) Can Redwood Private runtime support direct CloudHSM over their network (mTLS + HSM client libs)? Do we need a connector?
2) Which quantization kernels are validated on T4 with Llama2-13B q4f16 in our runtime? Any known p99 latency cliff behavior?
3) Is console RBAC mapping to SAML groups already supported in Private mode or needs custom work?
4) For immutable audit logs to internal S3, do we push logs from runtime or from control plane? They insist logs never leave their VPC unencrypted.

Notes / ad-hoc observations from call:
- Anil repeatedly emphasized "no external indexing allowed" — we must ensure any fallback to Redwood cloud Dedicated does not index their data. Must clarify caching policy.
- They are cost sensitive; initial ask: show cost delta between full A100 baseline vs mixed T4 + A100 with q4.
- They use internal monitoring (Prometheus + Grafana) — we should expose runtime metrics via Prometheus push/pull endpoints inside VPC.

Scratch config snippet (non-executable, for SE discussion):
- runtime.config: {
  model: "llama2-13b-q4f16",
  max_batch_size: 8,
  max_batch_latency_ms: 80,
  kv_cache_enabled: true,
  prefix_cache: ["system_prompt_v1"],
  audit_log_sink: "s3://redcrest-audit-logs/2025/",
  metrics_endpoint: "prometheus://10.0.12.5:9090"
}

Risk register (quick):
- Quality risk: quantization causing hallucinations -> mitigate with golden-set eval hook + fallback to float model on regression.
- SLA risk: cold-starts for new claim templates -> mitigate with pre-warming and prefix cache.
- Security risk: misconfigured routing could leak index pointers -> require network review and RBAC lockout.

Final notes: this is a high-touch enterprise PoC; likely 6–8 week engagement to productionize once golden set and lab benchmarks validated. Wide range of stakeholders: infra, security, legal.

---
TO DO (explicit for Maya): finalize SOW bullet list and include options (Private-only vs Private+Dedicated-burst). Add estimated costs (A100 hour, T4 hour, engineering scoping hours) and include clause for quantization QA support in Redwood Optimize.

End of raw intake.
